note: Every artifact the engine installer fetches on the node, by exact URL and SHA-256 (and size). `operator:FILE` artifacts come from the stage folder; the rest are downloaded by root on the node. All filled on the node rehearsal of 2026-10-17 (NODE.md section 8 A); refill with `python3 deploy/engine/engine.py pin FILE` when a pin changes. The model pins are the Kira 2 model checksums, confirmed against Hugging Face's x-linked-etag.

node.how: nodejs.org's own release; matched against its SHASUMS256.txt for v24.11.1 (node rehearsal 2026-10-17)

dsh.how: In an empty folder named dsh (the lockfile records the folder name), with the pinned node first on PATH: npm install --save-exact --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-alpha.5; then tar --sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime=@0 -czf dsh-engine-0.2.1-alpha.5-linux-x64.tar.gz package.json package-lock.json node_modules. Two runs gave these bytes; the package graph (613 packages) is the wall test's (/opt/toy-boundary/engine), name for name and version for version.

openshell.how: usr/bin/openshell and usr/bin/openshell-gateway from NVIDIA's openshell_0.1.4-1_amd64.deb (GitHub release v0.1.4, sha256 33045069ed26acb3d1550bf10297bf4eaf9e0dce4a8c19b0dab4564650daf921 per its openshell-checksums-sha256.txt; byte-identical to the binaries the wall test ran), in a folder openshell-0.1.4: tar --sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime=@0 --mode=go-w -cf - openshell-0.1.4 | gzip -n -9

sandbox_image.how: docker save -o openshell-sandbox-image.tar node:24-bookworm ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/sandbox:0.1.4 ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/supervisor:0.1.4 on the wall-test VM (docker.io 29.1.3, containerd snapshotter): the sandbox's root image (sha256:14078204b6bb...) and the two images the docker driver runs beside it (sandbox sha256:ca00c094aeaa..., supervisor sha256:aa681d8264af...). Two saves gave these bytes. The first name is the image engine-run.sh starts.

llama.how: the CPU build of the release the Mac runs (llama-server version 0.3.0, build 10621, commit c1d0e7a00); the release ships a tar.gz, not a zip; the sha256 is GitHub's asset digest

rust.how: RUSTUP_HOME=$PWD/rustup CARGO_HOME=$PWD/cargohome rustup toolchain install 1.99.1 --profile minimal --target wasm32-unknown-unknown --no-self-update; then, inside rustup/toolchains/1.99.1-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu: tar --sort=name --owner=0 --group=0 --numeric-owner --mtime=@0 --mode=go-w -cf - . | gzip -n -9. The toolchain folder itself, so /opt/rust/bin/cargo and rustc run without rustup.
